subject: Streaming response hangs -> websocket/chunked-transfer timeouts (Finovate)
messages:
From: Luke Barnes <lbarnes@finovate.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Major issue: streaming API hanging intermittently (production)

Marissa,

We're seeing a spike in failed streaming responses from Redwood's hosted endpoint (api.redwood.ai/v1/stream). Over the past 2 hours approx 5% of requests that should stream to completion are stalling mid-stream — the client sees no further chunks and eventually the socket times out. When that happens, our service reports incomplete outputs and downstream reconciliation fails.

Symptoms:
- Error rate on streaming route: ~5% (normally <0.2%) since 07:00 PDT.
- Many sessions show a final TCP FIN without any trailing chunk; others show a silent stall with no further chunk frames for 90-120s.
- We see WebSocket disconnects with code 1006 frequently around ~120s.
- Non-streaming (batch) requests are OK.

We've attached logs and a sample handshake trace. Can you escalate? This is impacting our live payment chat flows (Finovate Prod App).

Attached: logs_20260309.zip, websocket_handshake.txt

We need ETA and mitigation — can you convene your on-call and ops?

Thanks,
Luke Barnes
Director, Platform Engineering
Finovate Payments

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Luke Barnes <lbarnes@finovate.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Major issue: streaming API hanging intermittently (production)

I pulled the logs Luke attached and matched them to the streaming proxy traces. Quick observations:
- Multiple sessions terminate with no final chunk; the upstream model server logs show the generation completed and the last token sent to the proxy.
- The proxy (nginx fronting the runtime) shows connection keepalive closed at ~60s for some sessions and at ~120s for others. Some websocket sessions show no close frame.
- I also see small bursts of 502/PRX errors on the CPU-constrained hyperlane GPUs around 07:05–07:20. Could be transient capacity pressure + a connection handling edge-case.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low risk):
- Increase nginx proxy_read_timeout and keepalive_timeout to 300s in the streaming route. (Can push via config and reload)
- Enable websocket ping/pong at the proxy level and instruct clients to respond/ping.
- Route Finovate traffic to an alternative pool (dedicated burst cluster) while we validate.

I've attached a short trace snippet (heartbeat_trace.txt) and the websocket handshake.

If these changes don't reduce the incidents in 30–45m, I'll propose a hotfix revert of the recent streaming kernel change.

— Dev
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Luke Barnes <lbarnes@finovate.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Major issue: streaming API hanging intermittently (production)

Summary of findings after a quick debug:
- Root cause (likely): a regression in the runtime's chunk-flush logic introduced in commit 5f8b7c (streaming-optimizations). When the server-side output buffer is empty at an exact scheduling boundary, the flush path fails to emit the final zero-length chunk/termination marker in certain load scenarios, leaving proxies waiting for more data. Combined with aggressive LB idle timeouts, this manifests as a hanging stream.
- Repro: internal fuzz tests reproduce stalled stream when model latency spikes briefly and the runtime's background flusher doesn't run.

Mitigation plan (immediate -> short -> medium):
Immediate (apply now):
1) Increase proxy keepalive/proxy_read_timeout to 300s for streaming endpoints (Dev has the playbook).
2) Route Finovate to a less-loaded pool (we have capacity in us-west-2-burst).

Short (next 2–4 hours):
1) Hotfix rollback of 5f8b7c to restore previous flush semantics and deploy to canary (SUP-7342).
2) Add aggressive server-side websocket ping/pong (config toggle) to detect dead sessions faster.

Medium (next week):
1) Add end-to-end tests for chunked termination and increase CI fuzzing coverage.
2) Improve observability: create a streaming-sessions metric for 'no-termination' counts and an alert.

Schedule:
- Rolling config push + routing change: 10:00–10:15 PDT (apply now).
- Canary hotfix deploy: target 12:00 PDT after canary verification.

I have opened SUP-7342 and drafted the rollback patch. Attaching runbook link: https://redwood-internal/ops/runbooks/streaming-hangs-2026

Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
